routeSelection.basis: Language and Communication represents the broad degree through language in use, cultural diversity and public life. The Culture, Communication and Diversity core spans these areas. The second package uses the internship-based option rather than combining two communication packages with overlapping slots.

selection.assessment: The three selected plans meet the coherence and pairwise distinctness requirements. The other evidenced directions remain recorded as candidates at the three-plan limit.

alternatives.label: Literature, art and society
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the emphasis of the selected courses.
alternatives.concept: Use literature, art, film and history to study how societies tell stories about themselves. Compare texts and visual cultures, and use research methods to investigate questions about identity and public life.
progression: Introductory art, film and sociology lead into stylistics, cultural history and qualitative and quantitative methods. Literary foundations precede advanced interpretation and adaptation, and methods precede independent historical research.

alternatives.label: Film, media and digital culture
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the emphasis of the selected courses.
alternatives.concept: Study how film and digital media shape stories, public debate and identity. Compare media across periods, produce documentary and creative work, and use programming, text data and AI ethics to explore digital culture.
alternatives.distinctness: 8 courses and 60 EC differ each way from option 1. Film production, digital culture and computational and ethical perspectives distinguish this plan.
progression: Rhetoric, film and Python provide foundations for media history, qualitative inquiry, digital culture, data analysis and advanced media projects.

alternatives.label: Colonial histories, gender and cultural power
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the emphasis of the selected courses.
alternatives.concept: Study how colonialism, race and gender shape cultural representation and public life. Work with historical sources, life writing and media, and use political and social theory to examine inequality and resistance.
alternatives.distinctness: 13 courses and 97.5 EC differ each way from option 1. 15 courses and 112.5 EC differ each way from option 2. Empire, Indigenous histories, gender, rights and inequality distinguish this plan.
progression: Introductory history and sociology lead into gender history, empire, social theory and political analysis. Later courses apply these foundations to Indigenous histories, racial representation, public movements and independent historical research.

notes.text: Utrecht students combine an approved specialization and a second package with electives. This example fulfills the internship or study-abroad requirement through an internship. The degree also requires a portfolio.
Utrecht requires a communication research lab and a thesis in this pathway. The UCR options develop research through courses and include a separate optional independent research element.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

audience.programmeDescription: Study how language, art, media and history shape society. Utrecht teaches mainly in Dutch, with some courses in English. This example focuses on communication and cultural diversity.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Utrecht combines a communication core with practical humanities research and an internship. The UCR options focus on literature and art, film and digital culture, or colonial histories and gender.
